title: AquaWatch — Entity Relationship Diagram
system: IoT-Based Water Quality Monitoring and Predictive Alert System for Seabass Aquaculture
database: Firebase Realtime Database (NoSQL hierarchical tree — entities mapped to node paths)

entities.name: User
entities.description: A system account. Workers use the mobile app; admins use the web dashboard (see Admin).
entities.readBy: Cloud Function (push targeting), admin web app

entities.name: Admin
entities.description: Authorization flag marking which accounts may open the web dashboard.

attributes.name: value
attributes.description: Always true; presence of node = admin rights

entities.writtenBy: Firebase Console only (no client can self-promote — enforced by rules)

entities.name: LiveReading
entities.description: The current sensor snapshot — one per tank, continuously overwritten by the ESP32.

entities.name: HistoryReading
entities.description: Append-only time-series of readings — feeds trend charts and predictive analytics.
entities.readBy: Mobile Trends screen, admin charts, CSV export, predictive estimator

entities.name: ThresholdConfig
entities.description: Admin-defined safe ranges for each parameter — the single source of truth for STABLE/CAUTION and alert evaluation.

entities.name: IntervalConfig
entities.description: ESP32 sampling frequency, remotely changeable from the mobile app.

attributes.name: interval_seconds
attributes.description: Seconds between readings (10 s floor, default 15)

entities.readBy: ESP32 (applies within ~60 s), mobile/web freshness windows

entities.name: Sensor
entities.description: A physical sensor unit under lifecycle management (install → countdown → replace/remove).

attributes.name: removedAt
attributes.description: Set when a worker removes the sensor

entities.readBy: Admin web sensor dashboard, replacement-alert panel

entities.name: Alert
entities.description: System event log — threshold breaches (ESP32) and sensor lifecycle transitions (mobile app).

attributes.name: value
attributes.description: Reading that triggered the alert (0 for lifecycle alerts)

attributes.name: actionTaken
attributes.description: Human-readable message, e.g. 'Change water — TDS too high'

entities.writtenBy: ESP32 (5-min cooldown per parameter), mobile app (sensor transitions)
entities.readBy: Mobile Alerts tab (filters), admin Alert History, Cloud Function (triggers push)

entities.name: Report
entities.description: Worker-submitted incident report with photo evidence — the permanent 'log of what happened'.

attributes.name: issue
attributes.description: Main issue, e.g. 'Low Water Level - Tank 3' (presence of this field identifies a real worker report)

entities.writtenBy: Mobile app (manual reports + auto-logged sensor install/remove)
entities.readBy: Admin web Report Dashboard (Receive), mobile Report History

entities.name: SentMessage
entities.description: Message/task sent by the admin to workers.
entities.readBy: Admin web app (Sent tab); mobile reader pending decision

externalStorage.name: ReportImage

attributes.name: downloadUrl
attributes.description: Signed public URL stored in Report.imageUrls

externalStorage.readBy: Mobile Report History, admin web Receive tab

relationships.description: A worker submits many reports over time.
An admin sends many messages/tasks to workers.
A user may or may not be flagged as an admin (flag stored separately for security).
Thresholds define when ESP32 readings generate alerts (severity + 5-min cooldown).
A sensor's lifecycle transitions (→ replace, → inactive) generate alert entries.
Sensor install/remove events auto-log report entries; manual reports reference a sensorId.
A report may carry multiple photos (URLs stored, files in Firebase Storage).
Each ESP32 cycle updates the live node and appends an immutable history record.
Sampling frequency determines how often live readings and history entries occur.
Each new alert fans out as an FCM push to every user holding an fcmToken.
The TDS trend regression is compared to tds_max to predict the next water-change date.

notes: Firebase RTDB is a NoSQL tree: 'foreign keys' are logical (sensorId, uid, workerId strings), not enforced constraints — referential integrity is maintained by application code.
Rules enforce: users/{uid} self-access only; config writes admin-only (interval_seconds worker-writable); tank data requires any authenticated user.
The ESP32 authenticates anonymously (auth != null); Cloud Function uses the Admin SDK (bypasses rules).
